Title: Slide 1
Cell Biology: Structure and Function of Eukaryotic Organelles
High School & AP Biology | Comprehensive Organelle Breakdown

Title: Slide 2
1. Plasma Membrane and the Nucleus
• Plasma Membrane: Phospholipid bilayer with embedded transport proteins, cholesterol, and glycoproteins following the fluid mosaic model. Regulates selective permeability (homeostasis).
• Nucleus: Houses genomic DNA organized into chromatin. Enclosed by double nuclear membrane with nuclear pores.
• Nucleolus: Dense subnuclear region responsible for ribosomal RNA (rRNA) transcription and ribosome subunit assembly.

Title: Slide 3
2. Mitochondria: Cellular Respiration and ATP
• Structure: Outer membrane, intermembrane space, highly folded inner membrane (cristae), and mitochondrial matrix.
• Function: Site of Krebs cycle (matrix) and Oxidative Phosphorylation / Electron Transport Chain (cristae).
• Endosymbiotic Theory: Mitochondria contain circular DNA and 70S ribosomes, indicating ancestral bacterial origin.
• ATP Output: Generates ~30-32 ATP molecules per glucose molecule through aerobic respiration.

Title: Slide 4
3. Distinct Structures: Plant vs Animal Cells
• Chloroplasts: Thylakoid stacks (grana) containing chlorophyll for photosynthesis (light & dark reactions) in plant cells.
• Cell Wall: Rigid outer cellulose matrix in plant cells providing turgor pressure and structural support.
• Central Vacuole: Large plant organelle for water storage, osmotic balance, and waste degradation.
• Lysosomes & Centrosomes: Predominantly active in animal cells for autophagy and mitotic spindle formation.
